original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Answer Open next question 1 of PR3662 (research/ceiling-exp-fixed-point): compare its fixed-point exponential bounds with the pinned ceiling.py Taylor series for every rational argument in [0, 1/2] at PREC=256.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for faster replay without coverage loss. PR3662 keeps its faster kernel opt-in until equality with the pinned series is settled on the whole domain. This package settles that coverage question instead of measuring a new speedup.
bottleneck_link: An opt-in replay kernel can be adopted only with a precise statement of what it preserves. The theorem gives soundness on the whole domain and shows that byte-identical brackets are not guaranteed.
stop_rule: Stop at a written all-argument comparison theorem with explicit witnesses for every allowed difference; no change to either engine and no caller-wide argument census.
evidence: PROOF.md all-argument proof; three exact witnesses; 987 general and 391 stopping-threshold arguments checked against the theorem, index relations and an independent 2^-420 enclosure; exact loop replicas matched to both pinned engines; 13 rejected controls; warning-strict normal and optimized runs.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does the selected ceiling search, or another registered caller of ceiling.py, visit an argument where the engines differ?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This decides whether the kernel can be used there without a separate bracket-equality check.
open_questions.first_step: Log every exp argument of each registered caller and test the stopping-threshold and grid-proximity conditions of PROOF.md.
open_questions.blocked_by: Caller argument logs are not produced here.

open_questions.question: Can a fast path with an exact-rational fallback near grid points and stopping thresholds reproduce the pinned bounds byte for byte?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It could keep most of the speedup while removing the bracket difference.
open_questions.first_step: Detect the two proximity conditions from the integer state and fall back to the pinned series there; measure the fallback rate.
open_questions.blocked_by: No fallback kernel is implemented here.

open_questions.question: Do fixed-point atanh and ln kernels admit the same one-step comparison?
open_questions.why_it_matters: They have the same threshold stopping form and feed the same ceiling engine.
open_questions.first_step: Write the analogous index and rounding-error lemma for the atanh series.
open_questions.blocked_by: No fixed-point atanh kernel exists in the repository.

predecessor.author: Riquelme Soares (hevlyo)
predecessor.usage: Live input fast_exp.py, loaded unchanged; the open question is its Open next question 1.

principles: Build the Lever: one verifier loads both unchanged engines and emits a source-bound receipt.
Prove It Works: the replicas must reproduce both engines exactly before their indices are trusted.
Power of Ten: bounded loops (200 terms, fixed sweeps), explicit failure exits, no recursion.
deviations: Python big-integer and Fraction allocation is runtime-managed; arguments have denominators at most 2^420.
No Python static analyzer is configured for this package; warning-strict normal and optimized execution is used.
